data.title: US Black Friday online sales to cross $13 billion, Adobe says
data.description: Nov 27 : US shoppers to spend above $13 billion online on Black Friday, according to Adobe Analytics data, as bargain-hunting consumers look past inflation and high gas prices. Online spending on Black Friday reached $9.7 billion through 6:30 p.m. ET (2330 GMT), up 12.8 per cent from last year, according to Adobe. The final total is expected to land between $13 billion and $13.4 billion. • Spending is projected to remain strong over the weekend. Saturday spending is expected at $6.1 billion, up 6 per cent from last year, and Sunday spending is forecast at $6.4 billion, up 7.5 per cent • Cyber Monday is forecast to remain the season's biggest online shopping day, driving $15.1 billion in spending, up 6.2 per cent from last year • Across the five-day stretch from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday, online spending is projected to rise 7.4 per cent to $47.5 billion • Separate data from Salesforce showed Black Friday online sales generated $5.9 billion in the US and $30.7 billion globally in the first half of the day, keeping it on track for projected spending of $18.7 billion in the US, a 4 per cent growth year over year, and a 5.2 per cent rise to $83 billion worldwide • Adobe, which in September forecast Black Friday online sales would rise 9.2 per cent to $12.9 billion, expects US holiday online spending this year to grow at a similar pace to last year's

data.title: UK pensions minister says no evidence personal data comprised in cyber incident
data.description: LONDON, Nov 27 : Work and pensions minister Pat McFadden said on Friday there is no evidence so far that any personal details were compromised in a cyber incident which prompted his department to take some services offline. Asked whether the incident was a malicious act, McFadden said it was a "serous cyber incident", adding the investigation is ongoing.

data.title: US government bars bandwidth provider RETN from American networks
data.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 27 : The internet bandwidth provider RETN is being barred from US networks, the US government said in a notice posted to the Federal Register on Friday. Here are some more details: • The Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security said in the notice RETN poses "undue and unacceptable risks" identified in a 2019 executive order about hostile foreign IT firms. • The notice said RETN and its successors must "decommission and remove all equipment it has provided or installed either directly or through third parties from any U.S. network, and terminate services provided to U.S. persons" effective January 1, 2027. • Reuters' attempts to reach RETN for comment were not immediately successful. • On its website, RETN describes itself as a "Eurasian Network" with cables that tie Europe and Asia together via Russia. A 2013 press release describes the company as "a leading Russian wholesale telecom and backbone provider."

data.title: Commentary: Nvidia’s ‘great man theory’ is flawed
data.description: LONDON: For a tech industry so hell-bent on automating away humans, it seems perverse to celebrate the cult of the individual in the way it does. But that’s been the case with Jensen Huang, the disgraced boss of Nvidia, who came bouncing back after 11 days in exile , boosting his company’s stock market value by almost US$1 trillion on Monday (Nov 23). No other industry is as dependent as semiconductors on the intricate interplay between thousands of anonymous designers, engineers and manufacturers across the planet. Yet to many in Silicon Valley, the stock market and the White House, Huang is the chip industry.  “We have to protect our geniuses, and he’s certainly a genius,” President Donald Trump told CNBC, boasting of how he had persuaded Nvidia’s board to reinstate Huang.THE "GREAT MAN THEORY" Investors have good reason to buy into the “great man theory” of business, echoing the historian Thomas Carlyle, who argued that the “history of the world is but the biography of great men”. One of the most over-publicised yet under-analysed phenomena of our times has been the ability of inspirational founders to build remarkable companies that have defined new industries. Three of the top 10 most valuable US public companies are still run by their founders (Nvidia, SpaceX and Meta). That would be four if you include Tesla, driven since its early days by Elon Musk. Three more (Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon) remain heavily influenced by their creators, even if now run by non-founder chief executives. A punchy case for “founder mode” was made by the tech investor Paul Graham in one of his famous essays. Founders often had the vision, passion, knowledge and grit needed to run businesses that professional managers lacked. But, according to Graham, almost no management books or business schools had paid as much attention to founder mode as it deserved. It was sometimes a disaster for tech start-ups to switch from founder mode to manager mode and bring in outside executives, Graham wrote. All too often those “professional fakers” drove promising companies into the ground. Unsurprisingly, that narrative went down well among Silicon Valley entrepreneurs, raised on easy money, founder controls and Ayn Rand novels extolling the genius of creators and the flaws of “second-handers”.ALL COMPANIES WILL OUTGROW THEIR FOUNDERS But the great man theory of business, and history, has obvious limits.  No doubt history would have been different had Napoleon been killed during the siege of Toulon in 1793. But it is also true that Napoleon would never have risen to power had the French Revolution not erupted four years earlier. Similarly, Huang would not have built Nvidia into a corporate colossus without the deep learning revolution in AI. Times shape people as much as people shape times. Moreover, all companies will eventually outgrow their founders and have to revert to manager mode at some point. Some Big Tech companies have made a striking success of it. Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet may have lost the innovative spark they once had. But they have all added enormous stock market value since their founders handed over the management reins.On returning to office, Huang has doubled down on founder mode, dismissing the need to change his management style or plan his succession. Indeed, one person close to the Nvidia boss told the Financial Times that Huang should be asking: “How can I get some of those super voting shares so I can tell everybody to f*** off next time.” That would be a huge mistake. Whatever his talents, Huang has made some terrible errors of judgement that will continue to dog Nvidia. The newly empowered Democrats will hold hearings to examine whether Nvidia knowingly evaded chip export restrictions to China. The Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating the company’s accounting practices amid suggestions by Scott Bessent, Treasury secretary, that it may have pressed “seemingly illicit sales” to China to “goose” its revenues. And investors will still question whether it makes sense for Nvidia to keep acting as the central bank of AI as the market is cracking. Nvidia’s weathervane board is clearly incapable of enforcing governance. The S&P credit rating agency this week warned it may soon downgrade Nvidia over this lack of board independence and key man risk. And Nvidia’s share price has been sliding again.  For the sake of his company, Huang should himself work out the best way to switch to manager mode and hand over power. Founder mode does not cut it any more at Nvidia, and survivor mode would be even worse.

data.title: Explainer-Black Friday test for retailers as tight budgets meet AI-savvy shoppers
data.description: Nov 27 : Black Friday has evolved from a one-day frenzy of pre-dawn store crowds to weeks of online and in-store promotions, with retailers including Walmart and Target vying for more than $1 trillion in expected US holiday spending this year. But stretched budgets loom over the traditional kick-off to the holiday shopping season, as inflation rises and shoppers increasingly turn to AI to find the best deals and the lowest prices.  WHY IS IT CALLED 'BLACK' FRIDAY? In the early 1960s, police officers in Philadelphia described the chaos from suburban tourists descending on the city's stores the day after Thanksgiving as "Black Friday." The phrase did not describe a positive boost in retail sales until the late 1980s, when merchants spread the narrative of being "in the red" until massive Black Friday sales allowed them to turn a profit, or put them "in the black." HOW MUCH ARE SHOPPERS EXPECTED TO SPEND? The National Retail Federation expects US sales in November and December 2026 to rise 4.2 per cent year-on-year to $1.013 trillion, higher than the 3.1 per cent growth recorded a year earlier. Part of the estimated increase, however, is due to inflation. The latest Labor Department's Consumer Price Index report showed a strong buildup of underlying inflation pressures for the third straight month in October, amid rising costs for food and accommodation and oil price hikes due to the US-Israel war against Iran. The trade body estimates 182.7 million consumers will shop over the Thanksgiving weekend, down from 202.9 million last year. Several retailers, including Walmart, Ross Stores, Gap, Bath & Body Works and Lowe's, have also issued cautious holiday season forecasts citing uneven demand from selective consumers. A Deloitte survey showed spending during the Black Friday to Cyber Monday period is expected to remain unchanged from a year earlier at $624 per shopper, although participation was seen reaching a 10-year high of 87 per cent.  WHEN DO BLACK FRIDAY SALES START? Black Friday has increasingly become a weeks-long promotional period, with October events such as Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days and Target's Circle Week now kicking off holiday shopping. More than half of consumers surveyed by Deloitte had already purchased holiday gifts during the October promotions. Meanwhile, retailer Costco kicked off holiday promotions on October 30 and rolled out another round of deals on November 16, which are set to run until the end of the month. Walmart's "Deals & More" event started on November 12 and will run through December 2. Amazon and Best Buy launched Black Friday sales on November 19, with promotions running through November 30 and November 28, respectively. HOW ARE SHOPPERS FINDING DEALS? Consumers are increasingly using AI to compare prices, research products and scout for deals, with nearly one in five beginning their shopping with AI tools, according to Salesforce. AI and digital agents are expected to influence $75.8 billion, or 21 per cent, of global Cyber Week sales this year, the company added. Price comparisons and product recommendations are among the most common uses. Salesforce also said AI-driven traffic to retailers' websites has more than doubled from a year earlier, with shoppers arriving through AI referrals twice as likely to make purchases than typical e-commerce shoppers. WHAT DEALS ARE RETAILERS OFFERING? Electronics remains among the most heavily promoted categories. A Reuters review of retailers' websites found Walmart was offering an 85-inch Vizio Quantum TV for $498, down from $698, while Best Buy had cut prices for a 65-inch TCL TV to $229.99 from $469.99 and HP laptops to $449.99 from $799.99. Apple was offering gift cards worth up to $300 during Cyber Weekend, which spans Black Friday to Cyber Monday. Toy cars and racing vehicles such as Hot Wheels, LEGO sets and Barbie dolls, were among the leading gift picks in the toy category, an NRF survey showed last week. Retailers are also promoting beauty products, home goods and appliances, including a Blackstone grill at Walmart for $150, down from $224, and discounts by Ulta Beauty on brands including Sol de Janeiro, Tarte, MAC and Morphe.

data.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets
data.description: Nov 27 : OpenAI sued Apple on Friday, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology. The ChatGPT maker filed counterclaims in California federal court on Friday, saying that Apple's employment practices were designed to "trap" employees and prevent them from working on competitors' technology. Apple and OpenAI did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for talent and proprietary technology. Earlier this year, Apple sued OpenAI and two former employees, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT owner's foray into consumer hardware. OpenAI has denied those allegations. The litigation sets up a battle over who will control future AI devices that may not use traditional apps or operating systems — devices which, if successful, would direct consumer attention away from Apple's best-selling iPhone. Analysts believe OpenAI is working on a phone or other device of its own.

data.title: Exclusive-Volkswagen drags rivals Mercedes, BMW into $1.2 billion India tax fight
data.description: NEW DELHI, Nov 27 : Volkswagen has told an Indian court that tax authorities have wrongly singled it out over how it imports car parts at lower tariffs, alleging rivals Mercedes-Benz, BMW and Kia do the same, its latest salvo as it seeks to quash a $1.2 billion tax demand. The German carmaker has been fighting since 2025 to quash the record tax demand over allegations it "deliberately" imported components at a 10 per cent tariff and then assembled them into complete cars in India, evading the higher tariffs of around 30 per cent applicable on car kits. Volkswagen has denied the allegations, describing the case as a matter of "life and death" that could "wipe out" all of its investments in India, where it has just a 2 per cent market share. The dispute coincides with the German carmaker's challenges back home due to worker disputes over pay, and falling sales in its key Chinese market. After India accused VW of being the only carmaker indulging in such practices, the German company's unit in a non-public Mumbai court filing dated November 10 said "every manufacturer of comparable cars" follows the same "parts/components model" and pays duty at 10 per cent. If VW succeeds with its arguments about how its rivals import car parts, other carmakers could potentially face heightened scrutiny in the world's third-largest auto market. TAX DEMAND 'DESERVES TO BE QUASHED' "The contention that all other manufacturers paid duty at 30 per cent while the petitioner alone paid 10 per cent is unfortunate and factually incorrect," Volkswagen's India unit said in the filing, seen by Reuters, and being reported for the first time. The tax demand "deserves to be quashed for requiring the petitioner alone to pay 30 per cent duty while all other manufacturers pay 10 per cent," it added. To support its argument, VW attached a one-page table showing import shipment numbers of Mercedes, BMW, Hyundai's sister company Kia, Isuzu Motors and SAIC Motor's India unit JSW MG Motor, the filing showed. VW's India unit, Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, declined to comment citing ongoing legal proceedings. Kia declined to comment on Volkswagen's submission, but said it imports car components in accordance with applicable laws. The other rival carmakers it cited in the filing did not respond to Reuters queries, and neither did India's tax authorities. In an October submission to the court, seen by Reuters, Indian tax authorities described VW's conduct as one of "fraud and subterfuge". TARIFF DISPUTES LONG A SORE POINT FOR FOREIGN INVESTORS Tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors in India, as investigations and lawsuits can drag on for years, triggering business uncertainty. Global liquor majors currently are sparring with New Delhi over the tariff rate on bulk Scotch imports, though Indian officials say they are only enforcing the law of the land. In the VW dispute, India has alleged the carmaker shipped nearly complete Audi, Skoda and Volkswagen cars to its India plant but as individual parts and in separate consignments to avoid paying higher taxes applicable on car kits, and used internal software to manage such imports. After VW initiated a court challenge months after receiving a tax demand in 2024, Indian authorities told the Mumbai judge that other carmakers were paying rightful duty on their parts imports. VW SAYS IT IS BEING WRONGLY SINGLED OUT VW is disputing that argument with its own analysis, its latest court filing showed. BMW had 390,360 "major import shipments" of car components in 2024, while Mercedes had 80,972, all imported under the lower tariff rate category, VW said in its submission, without elaborating. VW is of the view that such a high number of component imports by rivals are also then used to assemble cars, just like it does, and so the carmaker is being wrongly singled out by New Delhi, according to two people familiar with the matter. However, a third person familiar with the dispute said for VW to succeed in its arguments, it will have to show that its rivals' imports were used to assemble complete vehicles. The court in Mumbai will on Monday decide on Volkswagen's challenge, but the people familiar with the matter said it is likely the court will for now only rule on whether tax authorities could have gone back 12 years in scrutinising VW imports or not.

data.title: 2026 in photos: AI, robots and new technology
data.description: Nov 27 : Technology advanced rapidly this year and long-anticipated developments in artificial intelligence, drones and robots appeared to be materializing, fast.  AI now permeates almost every aspect of life, from fashion and food to counseling and education, for good and for bad. In schools, for instance, teachers are having to rethink how they teach and test in a world of smart chatbots available to all. But AI-enabled technology can also allow medical students to train with virtual simulations, or help children who are hard of hearing understand science lessons. Illustrating technology through photography is not always easy. While robots certainly can be eye-catching — particularly when paired with humans in unexpected ways — concepts like AI or cybercrime often need a creative touch. Sometimes that might be through a glimpse into the world of the billionaire executives who run the big tech firms. Or it might be by documenting the backlash to the water-thirsty data centers springing up to power the AI boom, or by photographing in the bunkers of Ukraine where drones are transforming warfare. And sometimes, it just means taking really cool robot pictures.  (Writing by Rosalba O'Brien; Editing by Alexandra Hudson)

data.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets, FT reports
data.description: Nov 27 : OpenAI has launched a new legal action against Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers, the Financial Times reported on Friday.

data.title: Better fare transparency, support for ComfortDelGro’s taxi, private-hire drivers from Dec 1
data.description: SINGAPORE: Drivers on ComfortDelGro's Zig platform will have more transparency in their earnings and better support in cases of suspension or serious injury from Dec 1. This comes after Zig became the first platform operator to sign collective agreements with the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA) and National Taxi Association (NTA) on Friday (Nov 27). The NPHVA and NTA are both affiliated with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and have legal powers to represent private-hire and taxi drivers under the Platform Workers Act that came into effect in January 2025. NTUC secretary-general Ng Chee Meng called these first collective agreements with Zig a "significant milestone", adding that it might be a "world first"."They bring real outcomes for drivers, with greater transparency of their earnings, formal consultation before major changes are made to their work, and clearer channels to raise and resolve concerns," he said. Mr Ng, who is also Minister in the Prime Minister’s Office, added that Zig had set an example for the sector by being the first to go further than recognising Singapore's platform work associations to sign collective agreements with them. "We thank ComfortDelGro for its partnership and call on other platform operators to do the same for their drivers too," he said. He added that NTUC and ComfortDelGro have also committed to exploring how else they can work together, such as through company training committees.Other major platform operators in Singapore include Grab, Gojek, TADA and Trans-Cab's Smile. Advance figures by the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) released on Friday estimated that there are 57,000 to 59,100 private-hire car drivers and taxi drivers who did this as their regular form of employment in 2026. TRANSPARENT FARES The collective agreements signed on Friday cover over 15,000 taxi and private-hire drivers, according to ComfortDelGro managing director and group CEO Cheng Siak Kian. They represent an understanding between Zig and the associations on the terms and conditions of work for the represented workers. One outcome is to formalise Zig's existing practice of giving drivers a clear, itemised statement for every trip and payout. The statement shows what each fare is made up of, including surcharges and incentives, commission, payment processing fees, Central Provident Fund contributions and net earnings. "This allows drivers to check their take-home earnings for each trip and better track their overall earnings," NPHVA, NTA and Zig said in a joint statement. "They can then plan their hours, so they do not stay on the road longer than needed and can take regular breaks to look after their health." A minimum fare of S$9 (US$7) also applies to ComfortRide trips on Zig, which may be reviewed as operating costs and market conditions evolve, they added.SUSPENSIONS The agreements will also provide clearer recourse and support for drivers on Zig, said the joint statement. NPHVA and NTA members can raise grievances through the associations and escalate them to Zig's management. "For example, except in serious cases, Zig will warn or notify drivers before suspending or removing them from the platform, and members can appeal through their association and receive a written outcome with reasons," said NPHVA, NTA and Zig. "If a dispute remains unresolved, either party will be able to engage the Ministry of Manpower for conciliation and, if needed, the Industrial Arbitration Court." Serious cases refer to gross or serious misconduct, or where regulations require immediate action. The driver may be suspended while Zig investigates such cases. SERIOUS INJURIES Support extends to work-related injuries and other benefits. Drivers who hire Zig vehicles are already covered by benefits such as a personal accident scheme and rental incentives. From Dec 1, Zig will help eligible drivers apply for government-paid leave, including maternity, paternity, shared parental and childcare leave. Another benefit for Zig drivers will be access to health screening at preferential rates. These benefits, alongside other support measures, will also be made available to eligible private-hire vehicle drivers, said NPHVA, NTA and Zig. This includes drivers who do not rent Zig vehicles but take Zig jobs, and who are members of NPHVA and NTA.NPHVA is also separately in discussions with ComfortDelGro Rent-A-Car on more support for private-hire drivers who rent its vehicles. Extra support is also available for eligible drivers who are permanently incapacitated in an accident while doing platform work, and who qualify for work injury compensation. They will receive up to S$2,000 as interim relief on top of the compensation required by law. DATA-SHARING Zig also became the first platform operator to commit, in a collective agreement, to share data on drivers' work with the platform work associations. The business will share aggregated figures on earnings, online hours and completed trips with NPHVA and NTA. It will also provide "further information to verify drivers' earnings, monitor job trends and handle grievances", the associations and Zig said. Formalising such data-sharing gives the platform work associations a "stronger evidence base to identify emerging issues, track changes in drivers' working conditions and work with Zig on targeted improvements", they said in the joint statement.CONSULTATION ON MAJOR CHANGES Zig also committed to consulting NPHVA and NTA ahead of major work changes that affect drivers' earnings, allowances, deductions or working conditions, except in "urgent cases". It will also provide at least two weeks' notice of adjustments to fares, the app or pilot programmes. "In turn, the platform work associations will bring feedback from drivers on the ground, such as on job availability, operating costs and road safety, so that Zig can take it into account in its business decisions," said the associations and business. They added that drivers who rent from Zig are entitled to preferential commission rates. Zig was the first platform operator to formally recognise the NPHVA and NTA in February 2025. On Friday, ComfortDelGro's Mr Cheng said that ComfortDelGro will invest more than S$25 million over the next five years in welfare, benefits and expenses for its taxi and private-hire drivers. "A strong point-to-point industry depends on the people who keep it moving," he said.  "As we transform our business, we want the changes we make to create value for our driver partners and the communities we serve." NPHVA president Benny Lee Wee Beng, who has driven for a living since 1998, welcomed the agreements, saying that they made drivers' working arrangements with Zig fairer and clearer.He said NPHVA was in the process of engaging other platform operators to work on collective agreements. He added that the main challenge drivers now face is to increase fare earnings, as their working hours have risen from eight- to 12-hour shifts traditionally, to 12- to 16-hour shifts. "P eople are clocking 16 hours (on the road), which is very dangerous. So we really hope the fare of our drivers will go up, then we will have more income," he said.

data.title: Oil on track for first weekly gain in November on supply fears
data.description: HOUSTON, Nov 27 : Oil prices were set to snap a three-week losing streak on Friday, on track for their first weekly gain in November, as attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy infrastructure fanned concerns over Middle East supplies. Brent crude futures fell $1.42 to $95.20 a barrel by 10:16 a.m. ET (1516 GMT). Brent hit its highest since November 9 earlier in the session, but stayed shy of the $100 mark. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures at $83.74 a barrel were up 5 cents, or 0.06 per cent, from Wednesday's close. There was no Thursday settlement for WTI because of the US Thanksgiving holiday. "Attacks on Middle Eastern energy facilities and tankers have brought supply disruption back into focus," said Mark Schaefer, a director at brokerage Liquidity Energy. Prices retreated in recent weeks as investors were relieved that US President Donald Trump did not step up military action against Iran after the midterm elections. However, Iran has continued to attack ships transiting the key Strait of Hormuz, disrupting oil exports, while Yemen's Houthis have struck Saudi Arabian infrastructure. Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery temporarily halted some operations after a projectile struck it on Thursday, killing a worker, Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said. The strike was the latest blow to key Saudi facilities, a day after the Houthis claimed attacks on Ras Tanura, the kingdom's largest refinery and a major crude export hub.  OPEC+, which includes Saudi Arabia and Russia, is set to keep first-quarter 2027 output targets unchanged when the group meets on Sunday, three people with knowledge of the talks said. Separately, 10 people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the US administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC earlier this year and blocked Venezuela from paying its membership dues. Iraq is in negotiations with OPEC to raise its production ceiling as the country looks to develop its energy sector, oil minister Basim Mohammed Khudair said on Friday ahead of the OPEC+ meeting. "We think Brent can still push above $100 a barrel without another major escalation in the Middle East, but that increasingly requires evidence of constrained deliverable supply," ANZ analysts Brian Martin and Daniel Hynes said in a research note. Ukraine has intensified drone attacks on Russian oil refineries since the end of October, with the latest incident causing a fire at the Slavyansk ECO refinery in Russia's southern region of Krasnodar.  Separately, fires disrupted activity at Thailand's Bangchak refinery and Venezuela's Amuay refinery on Thursday. (Additional reporting by Florence Tan and Sudarshan Varadhan; Editing by Clarence Fernandez, Louise Heavens and Nia Williams)

data.title: Explainer-A million satellites? What SpaceX's Starmind could mean for Earth and space
data.description: Nov 27 : The US Federal Communications Commission authorised Elon Musk's SpaceX on Wednesday to deploy 1 million satellites to support data centres in space, a fleet that would dwarf the total number of active satellites currently orbiting Earth. The FCC said it was approving the SpaceX Starmind constellation to help meet rapidly growing demand for AI computing. SpaceX's Starlink pioneered the era of large satellite networks, known as megaconstellations, with rivals including Amazon and Chinese operators developing similar systems. But putting satellites into orbit on the scale envisaged by Starmind would take the boom to a new level, intensifying concerns among scientists about space junk, atmospheric pollution and the transformation of the night sky. SpaceX did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment on this story early in the US day. Here are some environmental questions surrounding projects such as Starmind: WHAT WOULD 1 MILLION SATELLITES MEAN FOR THE ENVIRONMENT? Scientists and regulators disagree over how much environmental damage Starmind could cause and how much can be known before the satellites, each with a wingspan of 75 metres (246 feet), begin flying. In a recent study, University College London researchers estimated that 1 million satellites could increase emissions from launches and re-entries by roughly 70 to 150 times from current levels. They said the resulting emissions could affect ozone, climate and air quality, and that SpaceX's filing lacked the information needed to fully assess those risks. The FCC, however, said those questions largely fell outside its remit. "Potential concerns related to the emissions of rocket launches and the subsequent impacts on the human environment as an indirect result of the Starmind system are outside of the Commission’s purview," the regulator said. It also dismissed concerns about satellites burning up in the atmosphere as insufficiently established. "Other concerns, including impacts on the atmosphere caused by satellites burning up on re-entry, remain speculative and not supported in the record," the FCC said. WOULD SPACE JUNK INCREASE? Almost certainly. Low-Earth orbit, where Starlink and the proposed Starmind satellites would operate, is already becoming increasingly congested, and experts say the amount of debris there would probably keep rising even if all space activity stopped today. As of February 1, there were more than 231 million debris objects in orbit measuring between 1 millimetre and 10 centimetres (4 inches), according to the European Space Agency, which has repeatedly called for measures to reduce collision risks. SpaceX told regulators in a later submission in response to the FCC that it would initially deploy satellites at lower altitudes for testing before moving them higher. It said onboard propulsion would enable collision-avoidance manoeuvres, station-keeping — keeping satellites in their assigned positions — and eventual deorbiting. The company also said it would continue refining satellite designs to reduce collision risks and use controlled re-entries aimed over oceans. SpaceX said its satellites would be designed to burn up completely during re-entry. But the sheer number of satellites changes the calculation. University of Birmingham professor Hugh Lewis said even a failure rate of 1 per cent could leave thousands of derelict satellites in orbit each year, which could increase the risk of collisions. WHAT WOULD HAPPEN TO THE NIGHT SKY? Scientists say it could change dramatically.  Following the FCC's approval, the American Astronomical Society said the proposed constellation would undermine decades of public investment in astronomical facilities and impair scientists' ability to study the universe.  Lewis said some of the Starmind satellites would be in "sun-synchronous" orbits and would always be illuminated, adding that they could contaminate astronomical images. Visual simulations shared online by Virginia Tech aerospace professor Shane Ross show bands of satellites stretching across large portions of the sky, potentially outnumbering visible stars. The FCC rejected requests for additional conditions, saying protection of optical astronomy falls largely outside its rules and that SpaceX's commitment to coordinate with the US National Science Foundation was sufficient. IS IT REALISTIC TO SEND 1 MILLION SATELLITES TO SPACE?    Not quickly. It would be impossible for SpaceX to launch 1 million satellites at the same time. The largest number of payloads carried by a single SpaceX rocket is 143.  Satellite operators sometimes request approval for higher numbers of satellites than they intend to deploy to buy design flexibility. For example, SpaceX sought approval for 42,000 Starlink satellites before it began deployment of that system. The growing network currently has just over 11,000 satellites in space. The FCC authorisation requires the company to place its first Starmind satellite into orbit by November 2033, have half in orbit by 2038 and complete deployment by 2040. No operator has ever sent 1 million objects into space. The proposed network is central to Musk's vision of moving energy-intensive AI computing into orbit with solar-powered data centres. However, SpaceX itself told investors ahead of its stock market listing that the ambition to build space-based data centres relied on unproven technology and may not be commercially viable.

data.title: Evidence of deepest explosive volcanic eruption found in Pacific trench
data.description: Nov 27 : An international team of marine geologists using a remotely operated submarine in an abyss in the western Pacific Ocean has found evidence of the deepest-known explosive volcanic eruption on Earth as much as 4 miles (6,500 meters) below the surface. The researchers sailed to the Mariana Trench, among the deepest oceanic valleys on the planet, to deploy a remotely operated vehicle, or ROV, called Jason/Medea. They used the ROV to study the trench walls around the deepest-known point of seabed on Earth, called the Challenger Deep. The ROV observed and collected pyroclastic rocks, telltale evidence of an explosive volcanic eruption composed of ejected rock fragments and volcanic glass. "The key findings are the discovery of recent igneous activity near the trench," said geologist Robert Stern, a professor emeritus at the University of Texas at Dallas and a visiting researcher at UCLA who is the lead author of a study describing the findings in the journal Frontiers in Earth Science. "Pyroclastic rocks are well known from volcanic eruptions on land and even in the shallow ocean, but they aren't known from as deep as we discovered them," Stern said. The Mariana Trench formed as part of a process called plate tectonics involving the inexorable movement of continent-scale plates on Earth's surface. The trench is the surface manifestation of a subduction zone, the boundary where one plate dives beneath another plate. The surface above the subduction zone typically has big volcanoes, but these are generally located about 125 to 185 miles (200 to 300 km) from the trench. The pyroclastic rocks that the researchers discovered were in the trench itself. The ROV explored along 340 miles (550 km) of a geological structure called a forearc that is part of the upper plate between the trench and a line of volcanoes on the seafloor, near the Challenger Deep. "The ROV was our principal research tool used for looking at and collecting samples from the seafloor down to 6,500 meters (4 miles)," Stern said. "We had a total of 10 dives, 7 of which were in the forearc around the Challenger Deep. The other 3 were in shallower waters near Guam because of weather conditions." The rocks collected by the ROV contained broken pieces of rock and volcanic glass cemented in a relatively strong matrix of finer-grained material. "This is unmistakably the product of a volcanic eruption. We did not see any eruption, and we have not yet found the vents from which the pyroclastic rocks erupted," Stern said. The age of the rocks is not yet known, but they appear to be recent, in geological terms, Stern said. The researchers are trying to understand how these explosive eruptions occurred at such depths, considering the vast water pressure at the volcanic sites. "The intense pressures at the depths that these submarine volcanoes erupted makes the eruption style different than it would be on land or in shallow water, where the pressures are much lower," Stern said.

data.title: Poland signs contract with Palantir worth $300 million over 5 years
data.description: WARSAW, Nov 27 : Poland signed on Friday an agreement with Palantir Technologies Inc worth around $300 million over five years to buy software that uses artificial intelligence to support decision-making processes by army commanders, Poland's defence minister said. • "This is a watershed moment for the operational capabilities of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Poland, Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said after signing the agreement • "We will use (the software) to build the best possible capabilities. All keys, servers, and information are — and will remain — the exclusive property of the Polish Armed Forces." • Poland started cooperation with Palantir in 2025, when it signed a memorandum of understanding covering artificial intelligence, information technology and cybersecurity • European policymakers had previously expressed concern that the continent was too dependent on US defence technology that could be cut off, limiting its ability to defend itself

data.title: China stocks surge most in two years as Beijing vows stronger market support
data.description: SHANGHAI: China's share benchmarks jumped 4 per cent and the yuan rose on Friday (Nov 27), after Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council meeting that called for a bigger role by "national team" investors to stabilise a falling stock market . Chinese stocks have struggled this year despite policy easing, reflecting investor concerns over weak domestic demand, a prolonged property downturn and uncertainty over the economic outlook hurt by trade wars and geopolitics. The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index ended 4.2 per cent up and the blue-chip CSI300 index was 3.7 per cent higher at the close, both notching their biggest daily gains since October 2024 when China rolled out massive stimulus measures to revive the market. China's tech-focused STAR 50 Index surged 15 per cent, the biggest one-day jump in two years. The rally also spread to Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Index gained 1.9 per cent while the Hang Seng Tech Index jumped 6 per cent. In Beijing's strongest gesture yet to support a stock market that had fallen to 16-month lows, the Cabinet said "capital markets were crucial to the broader economy", state media Xinhua reported. The Cabinet added that Central Huijin - the domestic unit of sovereign wealth fund China Investment Corp - would enhance its role as a quasi-stabilisation fund to ensure ample liquidity. The meeting also called for better policies to encourage long-term funds to invest in the stock market, and for measures to strengthen defences against risks spilling over from overseas markets. "It's a shot in the arm for markets," said Kenny Ng, a strategist at Everbright Securities International in Hong Kong. "Sentiment has been downbeat for so long. There hasn't been much good news to trade on. At least now there's something to count on: the national team will come to the rescue if things really turn south."The Chinese yuan gained 0.1 per cent against the dollar in offshore trading, reversing earlier weakness to hit its strongest in three weeks. The currency is nearing its firmest level in four years. "It's very rare that Executive meeting of the State Council would make such direct comments. Last time it happened was 2024 when they rolled out a liquidity support package," said Jason Chan, a Hong Kong-based strategest at Bank of East Asia. Given the current low investor expectations, any incremental supportive policies would help boost confidence, said Meng Lei, China equity strategist at UBS Securities. The latest statement follows the margin lending relaxation and trading fee reductions announced over the weekend, underscoring the government's growing determination to stabilise markets. LSEG data showed trading volume surged across broad-based benchmarks and sub-indices after the midday break, pointing to a sharp improvement in investor sentiment. The CSI Semiconductor Industry Index and the STAR Chip Index both shot up more than 17 per cent. Indices tracking China's AI, cloud computing and consumer electronics stocks jumped more than 10 per cent. But some analysts said it was too early to suggest the market was near a bottom as support from the national team alone was unlikely to lead to a sustained rally. "There is an increasingly clear signal that Chinese authorities are uncomfortable with the extent of the equity market selloff," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank. "I would distinguish between a turning point in policy resolve and a turning point in market fundamentals... A policy-induced bounce needs to evolve into a fundamentally driven recovery before we can confidently call it a durable bottom." Also on Friday, Xinhua Finance reported that regulators will launch a campaign to further tighten rules on share sales by controlling shareholders of listed companies. Regulators will also guard against listings by "pseudo-tech" companies, or firms that inflate earnings, the state media said.
